Goosebumps are your body reaching for fur you don't have 🐈

When you're cold, tiny muscles at the base of each hair contract and pull the hair upright. In animals with thick fur that fluffed coat helps keep them warm, and a puffed up cat also looks bigger to predators.

Humans have too little hair for it to keep us warm, yet it still happens with cold, fear, excitement and even music. In mice, scientists found the same system helps hair grow back.

Sources: Cleveland Clinic, NIH.
